items.source: specs/blink-RESULTS.md "String storage" (the alternative); research/BLINK-STRING-STORAGE.md; the ledgers of the merge's run, both configurations: painter `fail open`, reason `painted line wraps`; the painter owner's report of re-architecture step 3 (2026-09-19), "The two open painter rows"; the Blink owner's X3 report (2026-09-19) and specs/blink-RESULTS.md "Re-architecture X3", "A line painted in an RTL block" (48e058b); `.artifacts/tests/runs/ra-x3-blink/proof-after-b-no-facts.json` and `proof-after-b-facts.json`, whose `limitsDiffer` lists every case whose painter limits moved
items.note: Closed on 2026-09-19 (the re-architecture's X3, 48e058b). `engines/blink/paint-rules.ts` `lineStartScript.scriptsOf` takes the painted block's direction, which `paint.ts` passes at its three calls, and segments a painted line by script when its block is RTL. The two rows' painter status went from `fail open` to `fail covered by limit:script-at-line-start` in both configurations, so by rule they belong to `painter/named-limits` now. Tier 2 showed 8 painter transitions per configuration, all this limit: these two rows, and six rows that gaps already covered and that name the limit too (`c-2c3919e3066dac30`, `c-63105f8280e183a3`, `c-3ed24bee6c75ffc0`, `c-2b9ac66959add3b4`, `c-2d63e4cce5180b83`, `c-5b41281666ef0402`). No painted DOM changed. The limit moved in 461 recorded rows of each configuration (460 cases): named on 470 more lines and on 31 fewer. Chrome's references were recorded again and frozen at the X3 merge. The painted lines still wrap: no painted form gives Latin back, since no zero-width character has script Latin. What would reopen the item: one of the rows turning `fail open` again. What it was: Runs of 13 brackets after Arabic and after Latin in an RTL block, Amiri at 24px, 90px wide. The prediction passes lineCount, breaks and widths and is exact in both configurations since the rule for a neutral Latin range with a space (`shape.ts` `spacesStay`); before it the failing prediction's conditions covered the painter too. The painted line shapes its brackets otherwise than the paragraph did and wraps, and the painter reported no limit for it. Cause, found offline in the re-architecture's painter step (2026-09-19): in an RTL block Blink enables bidi (`inline_items_builder.cc:1744-1746`), so SegmentScriptRuns runs over a painted line of Latin-1 characters too (`inline_node.cc:1256-1290`), and the brackets take script Common where the paragraph gave them Latin. The painter's check assumed an 8-bit line is one Latin segment and saw no difference.

items.note: A prediction holds for the state it was measured in. Text measured before another paragraph's U+FE0E request and laid out after it is 1px per emoji off, with no condition on it when the facts are supplied. The round 4 critic's fresh set held 209 history-dependent Firefox cases (runs/split-word 87, word-spacing-spans 57, span-at-space 33, letter-spacing-spans 32) against 0 on each of the evaluator's three sets from the same generators; in file order 199 of them fail a prediction metric, in reverse 6, and counted, forward widths would be 98.21% instead of 98.97%. The Firefox line is for runs where this state didn't occur. On the tier sets the set was stable on 2026-09-18: the frozen recordings and the evaluation's, hours apart, mark the same 313 cases (314 on widths) in both configurations. The plain predictor's five cases (folded in on 2026-09-19 from the item `gecko/plain-predictor-fallback-state`, which named five of the cases above). In runs of the plain predictor (a paragraph prepared plain, the path an application runs) these five cases' NATIVE widths differ from the usual run's: fallback-font widths in another state, for example 33.5px against 18.5px for one code point of `c-56afde0f3d04b557`. Line ranges are equal, and the reference ledger doesn't mark the five history-dependent, because both orders of the usual run saw one state. They sit together in suite-sample part 2 (cases 1,078 to 1,083 of 5,000), where U+1F600 first meets U+FE0E, the text-presentation request that moves the process's fallback state. 120 cases of that part differ in all; the other 115 are history-dependent in the ledger already (`gecko/process-font-fallback-state`), and they hold all 14 whose line ranges moved with the native lines. The measure-first check moved the same five (with the lab's facts their widths went to `fail covered by page-history`). That browser process has two states: the usual predictor's five runs across X1 and X2 were never in the odd one, the plain predictor's were 3 times out of 5 (the set run again with it gave 0 differences once and the same 120 once). The Gecko owner's reading, which nobody tested: a predictor that asks Canvas less and sooner races Firefox's background character-map loading. A probe of that loading would settle it. Until then a native difference on these five under another predictor is this class. Under the usual predictor they pass every metric and are exact in both configurations. At X3 the plain predictor's Firefox run differed from the usual one in the same 120 cases as at X2, case for case, with the same five unmarked. Correctness round 5 (2026-09-19): two both-orders runs of the round's library, the Gecko owner's and the critic's, agreed natively on 74 cases of `heldout-suite-sample` part 0 without facts, and the owner's run with the lab's facts on 87 (the 74, 12 more on every metric, and `c-6403c221b98778d6` on widths alone: 86 on line count, breaks, the painter and exact values, 87 on widths). Those cases so read as going from history-dependent to pass. A plain predictor run an hour later landed in the other state: 74 native observations and 7 line ranges differ from the usual run in that part, the 74 are exactly the 74 above, and all are history-dependent in the frozen ledger. The critic didn't find what put that browser process in the other state. A pass in one recording isn't stable: the 87 are named here, and they stay this class whatever a recording shows them as. A new reference ledger that marks them as passes loses them from this item's rule, not from its names.

items.source: research/CORRECTNESS-ROUND-5.md, Gecko; specs/gecko-RESULTS.md, correctness round 5; the critic's sections 5 and 6; hb-ot-shape.cc:131-187; engines/gecko/advance.ts askedPlacement; registry rule `gecko/measure/probe-pairs-per-context`
items.note: What a probe pair shows is taken to hold for the face's other Latin pairs. The source guarantees it between GPOS and the kern machine, which HarfBuzz chooses once per face, script and language. It doesn't for a kerx table that holds pair and state machine subtables, nor for a GPOS second value record. A wrong verdict there carries no gap. No failing case: none of 1,008 installed faces does otherwise (the main-facts critic's offline study), and the round's critic's held-out probe has 1,781 of 1,782 told lines equal to the DOM, the other in the registered 1 au class. One Mac, DPR 2, pinned Firefox 156.0; DPR 1, another OS and the pref `gfx.font_rendering.coretext.enabled` are unchecked. Reopens on a face with kerx pair and state machine subtables for Latin pairs, or with a GPOS second value record.

items.note: Not an observation rule: the port already applies FloatQuad::boundingBox to element rects (lab/observe/webkit.ts boxRect), and the differing value is the width of the library's own `inline-box` display box. On a bidi line adjustVisualGeometryForDisplayBox starts from the line box's logical rect of the inline box (logicalBorderBoxForInlineBox, whose width leaves out a hanging trailing space), sets its left to the running edge L and its right to the running edge R after the children, and setRight is FloatRect::shiftMaxXEdgeTo: width = max(0, w0 + (R − (L + w0))), every step in float32. `c-cb91481c4f72e2ef` and `c-e13d8aa9e28342ab` to the bit: w0 33.33092498779297 (the Arabic word without the hanging space), L 94.92437744140625, R 133.87013244628906 give 38.94574737548828, which reports as f32(f32(L + w) − L) = 38.94573974609375, the native width; the library has R − L = 38.94575500488281. The members on lines without bidi content (`c-48c81e6d8f5d8d7d`: 41.15999984741211 expected, 41.159996032714844 native, the text box's own width on a centred line with a hanging space) go through processNonBidiContent and aren't traced to the bit. The fix is in rebuild/src/engines/webkit's display boxes (the inline box width on both paths, with the line box's width as the starting value), several lines with a new engine value, so it stays in the tail; the tier sets hold no such case (0 of 1,334 rich pre-wrap cases at their widths; 0 differing predicted values in webkit-host's frozen ledgers), the fresh sets 12 with the lab's facts and 1 without.
